subject: RE: Financial Controls & Resilience Questionnaire — capability mapping and evidence
messages:
From: Erica Barnes <erica.barnes@firstwestbank.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@regcap.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Financial controls questionnaire — initial request

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As part of FirstWest's vendor resiliency review, we need a filled-out controls questionnaire that aligns to FFIEC-style expectations. Our procurement/compliance team provided a condensed questionnaire (attached) that maps into sections for: business continuity & disaster recovery, change management, access controls, encryption/data-in-transit and at-rest, third-party dependencies, and audit evidence (SOC reports, penetration test summaries, and retention policies).

Can you provide:
- A capabilities mapping (where Redwood's product maps to each control and any compensating controls)
- Copies or redacted versions of recent SOC2 reports and penetration test summaries
- Runbook excerpts that show RTO/RPO targets and the manual steps for cross-region failover

We have a compliance review window the week of Nov 23; ideal to get your materials by EOD Nov 20 so we can route internally. If anything is redacted please flag the reason.

Appreciate it — Erica
Erica Barnes
Senior Vendor Risk Manager | FirstWest Bank
erica.barnes@firstwestbank.com
Office: (206) 555-0124

Attachment: FirstWest_Condensed_RFI_2026.xlsx

Subject: RE: Financial controls questionnaire — initial request

Hi Erica — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can meet the EOD Nov 20 cutoff.

Quick summary of what I'll send by Friday:
- Controls mapping spreadsheet (FFIEC-style) that crosswalks each question to Redwood product features, operational controls, and policy artifacts (will include notes on compensating controls where applicable).
- A redacted SOC2 report for 2025 and a summary from our latest pen test (third-party summary with sensitive details redacted).
- An excerpt from our infra recovery runbook showing our canonical RTO/RPO targets for the Hosted API and Dedicated modes, and the manual steps we use to promote fallback model variants and route traffic by policy.

I've looped in Monica (Security & Compliance lead) to provide the SOC2 redaction and Laura (Solutions) to help annotate service-level behavior for DR. Expect three attachments in one email on Fri.

If your team needs anything stricter (e.g., a notarized bridge letter or auditor-to-auditor transfer), let me know now so we can prep legal.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com

Sean / Laura —

Preparing the artifacts Sean promised. Drafts attached for internal review:
- FFIEC_Controls_Mapping_v1.xlsx (controls column, product mapping, evidence column, comment/notes)
- SOC2_Report_2025_redacted.pdf (PII and customer identifiers removed; auditor summary intact)
- infra-recovery-runbook-ops-v2.md (runbook excerpt showing stepwise failover, RTO/RPO, on-call escalation)

Key callouts in the mapping sheet:
- BCDR: We map Redwood Dedicated + cross-region fallback (primary in us-west2 -> fallback us-east1) to the FFIEC recovery controls. RTO typically 15-30 minutes for stateless hosted inferencing; RPO is near-zero for cacheless requests, and up to 15 minutes for stateful chat sessions depending on KV-cache window.
- Change mgmt: All model and runtime changes go through staged canary, automated smoke tests, and a manual gate for production rollouts >5% traffic. Audit trails kept in our change-log (see link).
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest with per-customer keys supported via KMS/HSM integration.
- Third-party dependencies: We list cloud provider regions, storage providers, and our model registry third parties; all covered in appendix A with SLAs.

Open items for Laura: please add one-line explanation of how fallback to quantized model variants impacts inference correctness vs. cost (comms for control justification).

Sean: once you sign off on redactions and the mapping notes I can bundle and send to Erica.

-Monica

Sean / Monica / Laura —

Received the package — thank you. A couple quick clarifying questions from our compliance reviewers:

1) Data residency & retention: Your mapping references per-customer KMS and mentions optional on-prem. Can you confirm whether Redwood retains any customer inference request payloads by default, and if so how long and where those logs are stored? We need explicit retention periods and whether WORM (immutable) storage is available for audit archives.

2) DR testing cadence: Can you confirm the last time you executed a full cross-region failover drill that included model cold-start timings and cache warmup? If you can provide the test date and a short summary of outcomes that would be ideal.

3) SOC2 scope: The redacted SOC2 looks good; our auditors asked if you can provide the auditor contact for validation (we can do an auditor-to-auditor vet if needed).

If you can reply to items (1)-(3) by EOD Nov 24 we should be in a good place to close our review.

Best,
Erica Barnes
Senior Vendor Risk Manager | FirstWest Bank
